seo.description: Fit-only wet room installation in Gerrards Cross. Tanked, level-access floors with a tested fall to drain. We travel from Bracknell, from £3,500.

h1: Wet room installation in Gerrards Cross

hero.intro: We travel out to Gerrards Cross regularly — the affluent Buckinghamshire commuter village near Beaconsfield and Chalfont St Peter is around 25 to 30 minutes from our Bracknell base, close enough that a wet room project there runs on exactly the same programme and standards as one closer to home. What changes from house to house in Gerrards Cross isn't the journey, it's the floor underneath: a wet room is the one bathroom format where the structural work matters more than the finish, because a drain and fall set out wrong before the tiling stage can't be fixed afterwards with better porcelain. That's true whether the property is a period family home or a newer build, which is why every Gerrards Cross wet room starts with the same unhurried survey rather than a template quote based on the postcode.

sections.heading: What the installation actually involves
sections.body: A wet room removes the tray and the step by turning the entire floor into the shower, which means the floor build-up, the fall and the waterproofing all have to be right before any tile is chosen. We strip the room back, check joist depth and how far the floor can drop or be built up, then install the drain and first-fix plumbing at the position that gives the cleanest fall — typically 1:60 to 1:80, set out with a laser level. The whole floor and walls to shower height are tanked, not just the enclosure footprint, and that membrane is flood-tested before tiling starts. Large-format tiles are laid to the fall from the drain outward, with lippage checked row by row, and the project finishes with a water test across the entire floor and a full snagging walkthrough before you sign off.

sections.heading: What we coordinate for a Gerrards Cross project
sections.body: You source the sanitaryware, brassware, tiles and screen; we handle the strip-out, first fix, tiling, plumbing and snagging from survey to handover, from £3,500. Because we're coming in from outside the immediate area, we build the day-rate work — floor build-up, tanking, tiling — into contiguous site days rather than splitting the job across visits, which keeps the programme tight and avoids a half-finished wet floor sitting exposed between fitting days. Protection for the rest of the house is set up before strip-out begins, since wet room floor work involves more cutting and screeding than a standard retile, and any debris removal from joist adjustment is planned in stages so it doesn't sit in a hallway for the duration of the job.

sections.heading: Booking your Gerrards Cross survey
sections.body: The £125 survey is where joist depth, achievable drain position and access for materials and waste removal all get confirmed for your specific property, before a firm quote is written. If the room sits upstairs we also check the ceiling below to anticipate any disruption there. From survey you'll get a written scope that separates the structural floor cost from the finishing specification, so you know exactly what you're paying for before tiles and brassware are ordered. Book a survey to start a wet room project in Gerrards Cross.

faqs.q: Do you charge extra to install a wet room in Gerrards Cross because it's outside Bracknell?
faqs.a: No. Gerrards Cross is around 25 to 30 minutes from our base, and our pricing from £3,500 applies the same way it does closer to home. Travel is built into how we schedule the job, not charged as a separate line.

faqs.q: How long does a wet room installation take in Gerrards Cross?
faqs.a: It depends on the floor build-up required and tile format, confirmed at survey, but the structural stage — joist work, drain installation, tanking and flood test — is usually the longest part of the programme, followed by tiling and a final snagging stage.

faqs.q: Can I supply my own tiles and sanitaryware for a Gerrards Cross wet room?
faqs.a: Yes — we're fit-only. You source the tiles, brassware, screen and sanitaryware, and we confirm the format and specification against the floor's fall requirement at survey before you commit to an order.

faqs.q: What if my Gerrards Cross property's existing floor can't achieve a full fall?
faqs.a: We'll tell you at survey, not partway through the job. Where a floor can't be lowered enough, a slightly raised threshold at the door is usually the alternative, achieving the same level, step-free floor inside the room.

image.heroPrompt: Purpose: hero image for the Gerrards Cross wet room installation page, showing a finished result rather than a work-in-progress. Subject and action: a completed wet room with a level, large-format tiled floor falling toward a discreet corner drain, a half-height glass panel separating the wet zone from a freestanding vanity unit. Setting and work-stage: a family en-suite in a substantial Gerrards Cross commuter-belt house, finished and in everyday use, late afternoon. Composition: three-quarter angle taken from just inside the doorway, the vanity and walnut-fronted storage filling the left foreground, the tiled wet floor and glass panel receding into the right background. Light and materials: soft overcast daylight through a frosted side window mixing with a single recessed downlight above the vanity, warm American black walnut vanity cabinetry against warm taupe large-format porcelain floor and wall tiles, matte black shower valve and towel rail, light falling unevenly with a cooler wash near the window and warmer tone near the downlight. Constraints: no people, no text, no logos, no brand names visible on fixtures, no LED strip lighting under every shelf or mirror, no catalog-symmetrical staging or twin fixtures, no single uniform colour wash across the frame, no plants, florals or candles as styling props, no shower shown running water, varied and believable surface sheen rather than uniform hyper-gloss.
image.heroAlt: Finished wet room with warm walnut vanity, taupe large-format tiled floor falling to a corner drain and matte black fittings, in a Gerrards Cross family home under soft daylight.
